note: Five designated primitive camping spots scattered along the area's gravel roads (Prairie Road, Cedron Road and the south lot), each one a small gravel parking lot in upland woods with the camping spot at its edge: no pads, tables or privy, so a rig camps on the lot. The lots run roughly 12-15 m wide and 20-35 m long. The only privy is at Johnson Lake, which has no camping. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - five Primitive Camping symbols on the map, each beside a Parking Lot symbol, five GIS points each at a lot's edge; the brochure counts 'five designated camping sites (no amenities)' and says camping is allowed anytime. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Every one is a lone small gravel lot; no main camp. Pin fine. Stored phone differs from the area page.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays, but every spot is a parking lot): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'. The brochure: 'five designated camping sites (no amenities)' and 'Camping is allowed anytime in designated camping areas. These may or may not have defined campsites. Seasonal closures and restrictions may apply ... Camping on other parts of the area may be allowed by special use permit.' The map (8/23/2022) draws five Primitive Camping symbols, each directly beside a Parking Lot symbol: on Prairie Rd north of Johnson Lake, on Cedron Rd at the west side, on Cedron Rd in the middle, on Cedron Rd toward the east, and at the south lot. GIS layer 27 has five 'Primitive Camping Area' points (OBJECTIDs 292, 293, 406, 295, 294), four of them within about 20 m of a lot's edge and the third (406) about 65 m from its lot at the edge of a field. On the 150 m leaf-off frames each is a single bare gravel lot in open woods, about 12-15 m wide and 20-35 m long, with nothing else: no pads, loop, fire rings or privy; a car is parked on the Prairie Rd one, and the south one has a small mown patch beside it. MDC designates a camping point at each lot, so under the 2026-11-09 rule it stays; nothing suggests 'camping in the parking lot' wording or 'not recommended'. A 23-ft rig fits any of the lots as seen.

CLUSTERS / MAIN CAMP: no main camp - five separate single lots 0.5 to 2.7 km from the pin (GIS: 38.78253,-92.59516 Prairie Rd, the pin; 38.77792,-92.59410; 38.77849,-92.58187; 38.77461,-92.57387; 38.75960,-92.58543 south). None is more than one small lot, so no split.
PIN: stored 38.78253,-92.59516 is the Prairie Rd GIS point, 13 m from the centre of its gravel lot (GIS lot 217 at 38.78243,-92.59524) and at the lot's north-east edge on the frame. No move.

ACCESS: 'From Prairie Home, take Route J west 0.50 miles, then Route W south 2 miles to the area.' The map legend separates MDC Improved Road from Unimproved and Service roads; Prairie Rd and Cedron Rd show as gravel roads on imagery. No ford, low-water crossing, 4WD wording or posted limit on the page, brochure or map. On the frames the Cedron Rd east lot's road crosses a small drainage just past the lot and the south lot's road runs beside a creek; I could not tell culvert from slab at that scale.
PHONE: stored 573-815-7900 does not match the area page, which says 'For more information call (573) 346-2210'. Suggest 573-346-2210.
WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront - stands): none of the five lots is at water; Johnson Lake (the largest of three lakes totalling 20 acres) has the dock and privy but no camping symbol.
